verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launches at approximately 17,000 mph (27,358 km/h).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'SLS will be traveling over 17,000 mph. That’s 23 times faster than the speed of sound.' (under 'How fast will the Artemis II SLS rocket travel at launch?'); 'the rocket goes soaring off into space at approximately 17,000 mph.'; R2: 'Speeding along at 17,500 miles per hour'; R5, R6: similar '17,000 mph' during ascent.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state SLS reaches ~17,000 mph during launch ascent just before orbit, presented as launch speed; km/h conversion matches exactly.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission reaches orbit before accelerating to over 24,500 mph (39,400 km/h).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Speeding along at 17,500 miles per hour... the ship needs just 90 minutes to complete one full, egg-shaped orbit... ICPS fired again... Escape velocity... 24,500 miles per hour'; R4: details ICPS burn after orbit to raise apogee for TLI.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm initial orbit at ~17,500 mph, then later burn (ICPS/TLI) accelerates to 24,500 mph escape velocity; sequence matches claim precisely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission accelerates to over 24,500 mph (39,400 km/h) to leave Earth's orbit for the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Escape velocity—or the speed Artemis II will achieve to free itself of the orbital pull of the Earth—is 24,500 miles per hour... translunar injection (TLI)—the rocket punch that hurls the spacecraft out to the moon'; R4: TLI burn after high Earth orbit; R5: ICPS accelerates to ~24,500 mph.
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly link 24,500 mph to TLI/escape velocity burn from Earth orbit to Moon trajectory; km/h approximate match.

verifications.claim: Upon returning, the Orion capsule hits Earth's atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the spacecraft will reach a reentry speed of 25,000'; R3: 'traveling at a top speed of 40,000 kph (25,000 mph)'; R4: 're-entered Earth's atmosphere at a maximum velocity of about 24,664 miles per hour'; R5: 'reentry speed of 25,000 mph'.
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm reentry speed ~25,000 mph (24,664-25,000 mph range, roughly matches); km/h approximate; minor variance but directly supportive.
